newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha mostly unchanged, wet trading dull.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha mostly unchanged, wet trading dull.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices drifted sideways in thin activity on Tuesday, traders said.
Bids for first-half May open-spec naphtha were heard at $215.00 per tonne, while offers were assessed $2.00 higher. The level was virtually unchanged from late Monday trade.
Second-half May was bid at $213.00 with no offers having emerged.
In spreads, second-half April/second-half May was discussed at plus $4.00/5.00, broader than Monday's $3.00/4.00.
The half-month spread from second-half April was traded at $1.85 between Japanese trading houses.
In physical trading, end-users kept to the sidelines in anticipation of further slides in regional naphtha prices.
Near-term naphtha prices have fallen about $19.00 per tonne in the last 10 days, reflecting weaker crudes as well as recovered availability for prompt cargoes. INTERRUPTED
